general_information.Description: Listening skill Upon completion of the course, students should be able to: - Identify listening strategies - Listen for main ideas - Listen for gist - Listen for reasons - Understand personal qualities - Understand jobs responsibilities - Understand complaints - Distinguish between facts and opinions - Understand vague descriptions - Distinguish between varieties of English - Follow the academic lectures - Recognise approval and disapproval - Understand ad messages - Understand business data - Understand sequence of events - Understand directions and telephone conversation - Identify purpose, attitute and solutions - Understand interviews and talk shows - Identify arguments for and against an issue - Listen critically to alternative viewpoints - Understand a scientific explanation - Identify a topic of monolog - Focus on pronuciation in each unit
general_information.StudentTasks: - Attend more than 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination - Actively participate in class activities - Fulfil tasks given by intructor after class - Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose - Access the course websites for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students and for practice and assessment.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: employ general grammar (of intermediate level) and business vocabulary to describe people, things and activities, to express opinions, ideas and feelings in various business-like contexts
understand and interpret information presented in verbal, numerical or graphical form;
listen to and understand others' talks so as to have appropriate reponses that help maintain and develop conversations and other oral exchanges for 10 - 15 minutes.
organize and present ideas and statements in a clear, logical and appropriate form of presentation within 10 minutes
read and understand various business-related texts including articles and reports of upto 1,000 words as well as, commercial articles
write e-mails, letters, memo, brief reports (upto 1,000 words) and other creative commercials
